description:
864 tiles at 16x16 for a dungeon of four elemental halls: coursed firebrick with live coals, faceted ice, a moss floor with roots, and fractured storm slate, all opening off one dark flagstone nave, with a rune channel carrying each hall's light out across the floor. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 611 of the 864 tiles are transitions — 71% of the pack. 13 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a 47-mask set missing three tiles is broken in your map and you find out while you are painting.
  • The halls meet each other, not only the nave. Four hall floors on the flagstone, four element-meets-element sets that form a ring (ember, rime, storm, bloom and back), four rune channels and a granite wall. Lay the halls in ring order and every corner where two of them touch has a real transition.
  • 10 materials × 4 variants on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so four halls do not collapse into one muddy dark. The smallest gap on the ladder is 16.0 luma, measured from the shipped pixels.
  • 56 objects across 105 tiles, one ornament metal per hall (iron for fire, silver for ice, verdigris for flora, brass for storm): hall gates, 3x3 floor sigils, statues and pillars, ice crystals and shard columns, coal heaps, an anvil and a cage, root knots and blossom shrubs, lightning rods, chests, urns, bones, a lectern and rubble. Each ships transparent, and grounded on every floor it belongs to with the contact shadow drawn.
  • 9 animated objects, 108 frames: a lit altar for each hall, a brazier and four founts. The silhouette never moves; only the light does.
  • A finished 40x28 sample map with 215 objects on it and every autotile set placed, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 40 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 988 files in total.

Two things to know before you buy

⚠️ The nave floor is Verdant 05 Depths' floor, byte for byte. If you own Depths, these halls, the rune channel and the wall lay straight onto the dungeon you already built, and that one material is one you already have. If you do not, nothing here needs it: the flagstone ships in this pack too.

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the animated objects arrive as static frames on pages B and C.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ — an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C/D/E object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 13 of 13 sets, 611 of 611 masked tiles, and 624 of 624 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame; 539 of the 611 transitions also fit there as loose stamps, and all of them are on the A2 brush.
  • Tiled — one .tsx per group, all 17 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 1,120 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 1,146,880 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4 — a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 17 atlas sources, 864 of 864 declared tiles built, 64 of 64 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 74 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete — exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this dungeon sits beside the others.

  • Verdant 05 — Depths — the dungeon, cave and crypt this nave floor comes from, byte for byte
  • Verdant 25 — Infernal — the layer below the dungeon: magma, ash and brimstone
  • Verdant 13 — Castle — the curtain wall, keep and gatehouse above it

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance — no diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
